text: A rectangle is a parallelogram with four right angles. The length of the rectangle is 9 meters, while the width measures 4 meters. Typically, length refers to the longer side of the rectangle, whereas width refers to the shorter side or the distance from one side to the other perpendicular to the length.

The area of this rectangle is 36 square meters, calculated by multiplying its length (9 meters) by its width (4 meters). This multiplication accurately represents the given dimensions and results in an area of 36 square meters.
The length and width of the rectangle are each 13 meters, making the total perimeter of the rectangle 26 meters.

A cyclist covers 120 meters in 20 seconds, indicating a speed of 6 meters per second. This calculation can be used to determine the distance traveled or the time taken, but it is not necessary to perform it here.

The average speed is calculated by dividing the total distance traveled by the time taken to cover that distance. Distance denotes the distance between two points, while elapsed time measures the duration or duration of time that has passed during the movement. In this scenario, an object covers a certain distance in such a manner that the ratio of distance to elapsed time equals 6 meters per second.

A cyclist completed a distance of 120 meters in 20 seconds, yielding an average speed of 6 meters per second over this period. The average speed, while providing an insight into the cyclist's overall journey, does not offer an accurate representation of their instantaneous speed at any specific moment during the 20 seconds. To determine the cyclist's exact speed at various points, additional data on their position relative to time would be required.
